hint_zh: 如果有啲買家真係鍾意呢檔自己嘅設計，佢哋會唔會因為幾蚊就全部走晒？
explain_en: Because the goods are differentiated, the seller is a price searcher facing a downward-sloping demand curve: raising the price loses some but not all buyers.
explain_zh: 因為啲貨係 differentiated，個賣家係 price searcher，面對向下斜嘅 demand curve：加價走啲客，但唔會走晒。

prompt_en: Entry barriers under monopolistic competition are low, so a new seller can join the market fairly easily.
prompt_zh: Monopolistic competition 嘅入場門檻低，所以新賣家都幾容易入到場。
hint_en: How much money and how many permissions does it take to open one more street stall?
hint_zh: 開多一檔街邊檔要幾多錢、要攞幾多個批准？
explain_en: Low entry barriers are part of the definition: the capital needed is small and no licence monopoly or huge economies of scale keep newcomers out.
explain_zh: 低入場門檻係定義一部分：需要嘅資本細，亦冇專營牌照或者巨大 economies of scale 擋住新人。

prompt_en: Which feature belongs to monopolistic competition but NOT to perfect competition?
prompt_zh: 以下邊個特徵係 monopolistic competition 有、但 perfect competition 冇？
options_en: there are many sellers in the market|entry barriers are low|the goods are differentiated|buyers can compare the stalls easily
options_zh: 市場有好多賣家|入場門檻低|啲貨係 differentiated|買家好易比較各檔
hint_en: Which of these does perfect competition already have?
hint_zh: 以下邊啲係 perfect competition 本身已經有？
explain_en: Both structures have many sellers and easy entry; only monopolistic competition has differentiated goods, which is why its sellers are price searchers.
explain_zh: 兩種結構都有好多賣家同容易入場；只有 monopolistic competition 有 differentiated goods，所以佢啲賣家先係 price searcher。

prompt_en: Which of the following is an example of NON-PRICE competition?
prompt_zh: 以下邊一項係 non-price competition 嘅例子？
options_en: cutting the price of every bag by $5|offering a 20 per cent discount for the whole weekend|redesigning the packaging and offering free delivery|holding a clearance sale at half price
options_zh: 每個袋減 $5|成個周末打八折|重新設計包裝，仲送免費送貨|半價清貨大減價
hint_en: Which action leaves the price unchanged but still attracts buyers?
hint_zh: 邊個做法唔郁個價，但一樣吸引到客？
explain_en: Non-price competition attracts buyers without changing the price: packaging, service, location and advertising. Discounts and sales are all price competition.
explain_zh: Non-price competition 唔改價都吸引到客：包裝、服務、地點、廣告。折扣同減價全部都係 price competition。

prompt_en: Why can a stall under monopolistic competition charge a little more than the stall next door and still keep some buyers?
prompt_zh: 點解 monopolistic competition 之下嘅檔口收貴過隔籬檔少少，都仲有客？
options_en: because it is the only seller in the market|because buyers regard its goods as different, so some of them stay|because the government has fixed its price|because it faces a horizontal demand curve
options_zh: 因為佢係市場唯一嘅賣家|因為買家覺得佢啲貨唔同，所以有啲客會留低|因為政府幫佢定咗個價|因為佢面對水平嘅 demand curve
hint_en: What makes a buyer willing to pay a few dollars more at one particular stall?
hint_zh: 係咩令買家肯喺某一檔多俾幾蚊？
explain_en: Product differentiation gives each seller a little price-setting power, so it is a price searcher with a downward-sloping demand curve, not a monopolist and not a price taker.
explain_zh: 產品差異化令每個賣家有少少定價能力，所以佢係面對向下斜 demand curve 嘅 price searcher，唔係 monopolist，亦唔係 price taker。

prompt_en: Under monopolistic competition each seller is:
prompt_zh: 喺 monopolistic competition 之下，每個賣家都係：
options_en: a price searcher facing a downward-sloping demand curve|a price taker facing a horizontal demand curve|the single seller of a good with no close substitute|one of only two or three dominant firms
options_zh: 面對向下斜 demand curve 嘅 price searcher|面對水平 demand curve 嘅 price taker|一件冇 close substitute 嘅貨品嘅唯一賣家|得兩三間主導公司之一
hint_en: Can the seller pick his own price, and does the quantity he sells change when he does?
hint_zh: 個賣家揀唔揀到自己個價？佢一改價，賣到嘅數量又會唔會變？
explain_en: Differentiated goods give the seller a downward-sloping demand curve, so he searches for the price that suits him; a single seller with no substitute is a monopoly and two or three dominant firms is oligopoly.
explain_zh: Differentiated goods 令賣家面對向下斜嘅 demand curve，所以佢可以搵啱自己嘅價；冇 substitute 嘅唯一賣家係 monopoly，兩三間主導公司就係 oligopoly。

prompt_en: Under monopolistic competition there are ____ sellers, and the goods they sell are ____.
prompt_zh: 喺 monopolistic competition 之下有 ① 賣家，佢哋賣嘅貨係 ②。
options_en: many|very few|homogeneous|differentiated
options_zh: 好多|好少|homogeneous|differentiated
hint_en: Count the sellers first, then ask whether their goods look the same to buyers.
hint_zh: 先數吓有幾多個賣家，再諗吓啲貨喺買家眼中係咪一樣？
explain_en: Many sellers plus differentiated goods is the standard definition; very few sellers gives oligopoly and homogeneous goods gives perfect competition.
explain_zh: 好多賣家加 differentiated goods 就係標準定義；好少賣家係 oligopoly，homogeneous goods 就係 perfect competition。

prompt_en: Changing the packaging, improving the service and advertising are forms of ____ competition, while cutting the price of the goods is ____ competition.
prompt_zh: 轉包裝、改善服務同賣廣告，都係 ① competition；減低貨品價錢就係 ② competition。
options_en: non-price|price|entry|market
options_zh: non-price|price|entry|market
hint_en: Ask whether the price tag itself changes.
hint_zh: 問吓個價錢牌本身有冇變？
explain_en: Non-price competition attracts buyers while the price is unchanged; price competition works through the price itself, and it is common under monopolistic competition to compete on design and service.
explain_zh: Non-price competition 係喺唔改價嘅情況下吸客；price competition 就係直接用個價，而 monopolistic competition 好常見用設計同服務嚟競爭。

prompt_en: Sort each way of competing used by the stalls:
prompt_zh: 將檔口用嘅競爭方法分類：
options_en: price competition|non-price competition
options_zh: price competition|non-price competition
items_en: selling at $10 below the stall next door|printing an eye-catching paper bag with the stall's own logo|offering a buy-two-get-one-free deal|moving to a busier corner of the street|letting buyers exchange goods within seven days|announcing a half-price closing-down sale
items_zh: 賣到平隔籬檔 $10|印一個有自己標誌嘅搶眼紙袋|買二送一|搬去街上人流多啲嘅轉角位|俾買家七日內換貨|宣布半價清貨
hint_en: Does this method change the price the buyer pays, or something else?
hint_zh: 呢個方法改變咗買家俾嘅價錢，定係改變咗其他嘢？
explain_en: A buy-two-get-one-free deal and a sale both lower the effective price, so they are price competition; packaging, location and after-sale service leave the price alone.
explain_zh: 買二送一同減價都係拉低咗實際價錢，所以屬於 price competition；包裝、地點同售後服務就冇郁個價。

prompt_en: Sort each characteristic into the market structure it describes:
prompt_zh: 將以下特徵分類到佢描述緊嘅市場結構：
options_en: perfect competition|monopolistic competition
options_zh: perfect competition|monopolistic competition
items_en: homogeneous goods|differentiated goods|every seller is a price taker|each seller is a price searcher with a little price-setting power|heavy competition through packaging, service and advertising|all the sellers must charge the same price
items_zh: homogeneous goods|differentiated goods|每個賣家都係 price taker|每個賣家都係有少少定價能力嘅 price searcher|用包裝、服務同廣告激烈競爭|所有賣家都要收同一個價
hint_en: Are the goods identical, and does the seller have any say over his own price?
hint_zh: 啲貨係咪一模一樣？賣家對自己個價有冇話事權？
explain_en: Both have many sellers and easy entry, so the dividing line is whether the goods are differentiated and therefore whether the seller is a price taker or a price searcher.
explain_zh: 兩者都係好多賣家、容易入場，所以分界線係啲貨係咪 differentiated，跟住決定個賣家係 price taker 定 price searcher。

prompt_en: Put in order what happens when a Ladies Street stall selling its own printed tote bags raises its price:
prompt_zh: 排出女人街一檔賣自家印花袋嘅檔口加價之後發生嘅次序：
items_en: the stall raises the price of its own printed tote bag by $10|some buyers switch to the similar bags at other stalls|the quantity sold falls, but it does not fall to zero|buyers who prefer this stall's own design keep buying at the higher price
items_zh: 檔口將自家印花袋加價 $10|有啲買家轉去其他檔買相似嘅袋|賣到嘅數量減少，但唔會跌到零|偏好呢檔設計嘅買家照樣用新價錢買
hint_en: Who leaves first when the price goes up, and who stays?
hint_zh: 加價之後邊啲人先走？邊啲人會留低？
explain_en: A price searcher faces a downward-sloping demand curve: a higher price loses the buyers who see the bags as close substitutes but keeps those who value the differentiation.
explain_zh: Price searcher 面對向下斜嘅 demand curve：加價會走咗覺得啲袋差唔多嘅買家，但留得住重視差異化嗰班客。

prompt_en: (Fictional) On Ladies Street, Ah Ling's stall sells tote bags hand-printed with her own label. About 40 other stalls sell bags that look similar but are not the same, and anyone with a few thousand dollars can rent a pitch and start selling. Which market structure does this describe?
prompt_zh: （虛構）女人街阿玲檔賣自己手印招紙嘅布袋。大約另外 40 檔賣款式相似但唔完全一樣嘅袋，而且任何人夾到幾千蚊都可以租個位開檔。呢個係邊種市場結構？
options_en: perfect competition|monopoly|oligopoly|monopolistic competition
options_zh: perfect competition|monopoly|oligopoly|monopolistic competition
hint_en: Count the sellers, look at whether the bags are identical, and ask how hard it is to enter.
hint_zh: 數吓幾多個賣家，睇吓啲袋係咪一模一樣，再諗吓入場有幾難？
explain_en: Many sellers, differentiated goods and low entry barriers together define monopolistic competition; identical goods would make it perfect competition and a few dominant sellers would make it oligopoly.
explain_zh: 好多賣家、differentiated goods 同低入場門檻加埋就係 monopolistic competition；如果啲貨一模一樣就係 perfect competition，如果得幾間主導就係 oligopoly。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each action taken by a Ladies Street stall this month:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將女人街一檔今個月做嘅事分類：
options_en: price competition|non-price competition
options_zh: price competition|non-price competition
items_en: marking every scarf down from $60 to $45|printing a new cloth label sewn inside each bag|handing out leaflets at the street entrance|giving a $20 rebate to anyone who buys three items|staying open two hours later than the other stalls
items_zh: 將每條頸巾由 $60 減到 $45|喺每個袋入面車多個新布招紙|喺街口派傳單|買三件回贈 $20|比其他檔遲兩個鐘先收檔
hint_en: Does the buyer pay a different amount of money, or get something else?
hint_zh: 買家俾嘅錢數有冇變？定係佢攞到其他嘢？
explain_en: A mark-down and a rebate both change the money the buyer hands over, so they are price competition; labels, leaflets and longer opening hours attract buyers without touching the price.
explain_zh: 減價同回贈都改變咗買家俾出嘅錢，所以係 price competition；招紙、傳單同延長營業時間就冇郁個價都吸到客。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A Ladies Street stall raises the price of its own design of hair clip from $50 to $60 and weekly sales fall from 200 to 150 pieces. Total revenue changes from $10,000 to $____, so its total revenue ____ after the price rise.
prompt_zh: （虛構）女人街一檔將自己設計嘅髮夾由 $50 加到 $60，每星期銷量由 200 件跌到 150 件。Total revenue 由 $10,000 變成 $①，即係加價之後 total revenue ②。
options_en: 9,000|12,000|falls|rises
hint_en: Work out price times quantity for each case before comparing them.
hint_zh: 先分別計吓價錢乘數量，再比較？
explain_en: 60 times 150 is 9,000, which is less than 50 times 200 equals 10,000; a price searcher sells less when it raises the price, so total revenue can fall.
explain_zh: 60 乘 150 等於 9,000，細過 50 乘 200 等於 10,000；price searcher 加價會賣少啲，所以 total revenue 可以跌。

prompt_en: (Fictional) On a fictional Ladies Street, stall A sells its own printed T-shirt at $75 and stall B sells its own printed T-shirt at $68, and both keep their regular buyers. Which conclusion is best supported?
prompt_zh: （虛構）喺虛構女人街，A 檔自己印嘅 T 恤賣 $75，B 檔自己印嘅賣 $68，兩檔都留得住自己嘅熟客。以下邊個結論最有根據？
options_en: the two stalls are in perfect competition|stall A must be a monopoly because it charges more|the goods are differentiated, so each stall is a price searcher|the market price has not yet been reached
options_zh: 兩檔處於 perfect competition|A 檔一定係 monopoly，因為佢收貴啲|啲貨係 differentiated，所以每檔都係 price searcher|個 market price 仲未形成
hint_en: In which structure could two sellers charge different prices and both survive?
hint_zh: 邊種結構之下，兩個賣家收唔同價都可以生存？
explain_en: Under perfect competition a single market price rules and the dearer seller sells nothing; different prices with loyal buyers on both sides show differentiated goods and price-searching sellers.
explain_zh: Perfect competition 之下得一個 market price，收貴嗰個賣唔出；兩邊收唔同價又各有熟客，正正顯示啲貨 differentiated，啲賣家係 price searcher。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ah Ling's stall has the best corner pitch on Ladies Street and sells more bags than any other stall, so her stall is a monopoly.
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿玲檔喺女人街最好嘅轉角位，賣出嘅袋多過任何一檔，所以佢檔係 monopoly。
hint_en: Are there other stalls selling close substitutes for her bags?
hint_zh: 仲有冇其他檔賣緊同佢啲袋差唔多嘅貨？
explain_en: A monopoly needs a single seller of a good with no close substitute; being the biggest seller among 40 stalls selling similar bags is still monopolistic competition.
explain_zh: Monopoly 要求係一件冇 close substitute 嘅貨品嘅唯一賣家；喺 40 檔賣相似袋入面做到最大，都仲係 monopolistic competition。

prompt_en: In an oligopoly a few dominant sellers supply most of the market, although some small sellers may also exist.
prompt_zh: 喺 oligopoly 入面，幾間主導賣家供應市場大部分，不過仲可以有啲細賣家存在。
hint_en: Does the definition say how many sellers there are in total, or who supplies most of the market?
hint_zh: 個定義講緊總共幾多個賣家，定係講邊個供應市場大部分？
explain_en: Oligopoly is defined by a few DOMINANT sellers holding most of the market share, not by a literal total of only a few firms.
explain_zh: Oligopoly 嘅定義係幾間主導賣家佔咗大部分市場份額，唔係話成個市場字面上只有幾間公司。

prompt_en: Oligopolists can ignore what their rivals will do when they decide on a price.
prompt_zh: Oligopolist 定價嘅時候可以唔理對手會點做。
hint_en: If there are only three big sellers, whose reaction decides whether your price cut works?
hint_zh: 如果得三間大賣家，你減價有冇效，係邊個嘅反應話事？
explain_en: Interdependence is a defining feature of oligopoly: with few dominant sellers, each firm's result depends on how the others react.
explain_zh: Interdependence 係 oligopoly 嘅定義特徵：主導賣家咁少，每間公司嘅結果都取決於其他公司點反應。

prompt_en: Prices in an oligopoly tend to be rigid.
prompt_zh: Oligopoly 入面啲價錢傾向係 rigid。
hint_en: What would happen to a firm's market share and revenue if a price cut were matched at once?
hint_zh: 如果一減價對手即刻跟，間公司嘅市場份額同收入會點？
explain_en: A price cut is matched by rivals and a price rise is not followed, so firms gain little either way and prices stay where they are.
explain_zh: 減價對手會跟，加價對手唔跟，兩邊都冇乜著數，所以啲價錢就維持唔變。

prompt_en: Which statement best describes an oligopoly?
prompt_zh: 以下邊句最準確咁描述 oligopoly？
options_en: a single seller of a good with no close substitute|a few dominant sellers supplying most of the market|very many small sellers of homogeneous goods|many sellers of differentiated goods with low entry barriers
options_zh: 一件冇 close substitute 嘅貨品嘅唯一賣家|幾間主導賣家供應市場大部分|非常多細賣家賣 homogeneous goods|好多賣家賣 differentiated goods，入場門檻低
hint_en: How much of the market do the biggest sellers hold?
hint_zh: 最大嗰幾間賣家佔咗市場幾多？
explain_en: A single seller is monopoly, very many small sellers is perfect competition, and many sellers with easy entry is monopolistic competition; a few dominant sellers is oligopoly.
explain_zh: 唯一賣家係 monopoly，非常多細賣家係 perfect competition，好多賣家加容易入場係 monopolistic competition；幾間主導賣家先係 oligopoly。

prompt_en: Why do the dominant firms in an oligopoly seldom start a price war?
prompt_zh: 點解 oligopoly 入面嘅主導公司好少開價格戰？
options_en: the law forbids them to cut prices|buyers do not care about price at all|rivals will match the cut, so each firm ends up with about the same share but lower revenue|their costs are fixed and cannot change
options_zh: 法律禁止佢哋減價|買家完全唔理個價|對手會跟住減，最後各間嘅份額差唔多，但收入就低咗|佢哋嘅成本固定唔會變
hint_en: If everyone cuts by the same amount, who has gained any customers?
hint_zh: 如果個個都減同樣咁多，邊個搶到客？
explain_en: Interdependence means a price cut is matched, leaving market shares unchanged while every firm earns less, which is why prices stay rigid and competition shifts to non-price methods.
explain_zh: Interdependence 即係一減價對手就跟，份額冇變但個個都賺少咗，所以價錢維持 rigid，競爭就轉去 non-price 嘅方法。

prompt_en: Interdependence in an oligopoly means that:
prompt_zh: Oligopoly 入面嘅 interdependence 即係：
options_en: the firms must share their profits with one another|each firm must consider how its rivals will react before it acts|all the firms are owned by the same person|the firms sell in completely separate markets
options_zh: 啲公司要互相分利潤|每間公司行動之前都要諗埋對手會點反應|所有公司都係同一個人擁有|啲公司喺完全分開嘅市場賣嘢
hint_en: With so few big sellers, does one firm's decision reach the others?
hint_zh: 大賣家咁少，一間公司嘅決定會唔會影響到其他？
explain_en: With only a few dominant sellers, one firm's price or output decision noticeably affects the others, so each must anticipate their reactions.
explain_zh: 主導賣家咁少，一間公司嘅價錢或產量決定會明顯影響其他公司，所以每間都要預先估對手點反應。

prompt_en: Which of the following helps to keep an oligopoly in place by blocking new entrants?
prompt_zh: 以下邊一項擋住新加入者，令 oligopoly 維持落去？
options_en: homogeneous goods|free entry into and exit from the market|perfect market information|huge set-up costs and long-established brand names built by heavy advertising
options_zh: homogeneous goods|自由進出市場|perfect market information|巨大嘅開辦成本同埋落重本廣告建立咗好耐嘅品牌
hint_en: What would a newcomer have to spend before it could compete at all?
hint_zh: 一個新入場者要先使幾多錢，先至競爭得起？
explain_en: High entry barriers such as huge set-up costs and established brands are part of the definition of oligopoly; free entry and perfect information belong to perfect competition.
explain_zh: 高入場門檻，例如巨大開辦成本同已建立嘅品牌，係 oligopoly 定義一部分；自由入場同完全資訊係 perfect competition 嘅嘢。

prompt_en: An oligopoly is a market with a ____ number of dominant sellers and ____ entry barriers.
prompt_zh: Oligopoly 係一個有 ① 數目主導賣家、而且入場門檻 ② 嘅市場。
options_en: small|very large|high|low
options_zh: 少|好大|高|低
hint_en: How many firms hold most of the market, and how easy is it for a newcomer to join them?
hint_zh: 幾多間公司佔咗市場大部分？新人加入又有幾容易？
explain_en: A small number of dominant sellers plus high entry barriers is the standard definition; low entry barriers would make it monopolistic competition.
explain_zh: 少數主導賣家加高入場門檻就係標準定義；入場門檻低就變咗 monopolistic competition。

prompt_en: Because each firm must watch its rivals before acting, oligopolists show ____, and as a result their prices tend to be ____.
prompt_zh: 因為每間公司行動前都要睇實對手，oligopolist 之間有 ①，結果佢哋啲價錢傾向 ②。
options_en: interdependence|independence|rigid|flexible
options_zh: interdependence|independence|rigid|有彈性
hint_en: What is the relationship between the few big firms, and what does it do to price changes?
hint_zh: 幾間大公司之間係咩關係？呢個關係對改價有咩影響？
explain_en: Interdependence makes a price cut pointless because it is matched, so oligopoly prices stay rigid and rivalry moves to non-price competition.
explain_zh: Interdependence 令減價冇意思，因為對手會跟，所以 oligopoly 嘅價錢 rigid，競爭轉去 non-price competition。

prompt_en: Sort each market into its structure:
prompt_zh: 將以下市場分類：
options_en: oligopoly|monopolistic competition
options_zh: oligopoly|monopolistic competition
items_en: four large chains supplying almost all of the district's supermarket sales|dozens of small stalls each selling its own designs of hair clips|three firms supplying nearly all the mobile network service in a city|many small noodle shops each with its own recipe and shop sign|a few large importers supplying most of the aquarium equipment
items_zh: 四間大連鎖供應成區差唔多所有超市銷售|幾十檔細檔各自賣自己設計嘅髮夾|三間公司供應全市差唔多所有流動網絡服務|好多細麵舖各有自己嘅配方同招牌|幾間大入口商供應大部分魚缸設備
hint_en: Do a few sellers hold most of the market, or is the market spread over many small ones?
hint_zh: 係咪得幾個賣家佔咗大部分市場？定係分散喺好多細賣家度？
explain_en: Oligopoly turns on a few dominant sellers with high entry barriers; monopolistic competition has many sellers, differentiated goods and easy entry.
explain_zh: Oligopoly 睇嘅係幾間主導賣家同高入場門檻；monopolistic competition 就係好多賣家、differentiated goods、容易入場。

prompt_en: Sort each statement about oligopoly:
prompt_zh: 將以下關於 oligopoly 嘅句子分類：
options_en: true of oligopoly|not true of oligopoly
options_zh: oligopoly 係咁|oligopoly 唔係咁
items_en: a few dominant sellers supply most of the market|entry barriers are very low|each firm considers its rivals before changing its price|non-price competition such as advertising is common|every firm is a price taker|no small firm can exist in the market at all
items_zh: 幾間主導賣家供應市場大部分|入場門檻好低|每間公司改價前都會考慮對手|好常見用廣告等 non-price competition|每間公司都係 price taker|市場上完全唔可以有細公司存在
hint_en: Check each sentence against the definition of a few dominant sellers with high entry barriers.
hint_zh: 逐句對返「幾間主導賣家加高入場門檻」個定義嚟睇吓？
explain_en: Oligopolists are price searchers, entry barriers are high, and small firms may still exist beside the dominant ones; dominance, interdependence and non-price competition are the real features.
explain_zh: Oligopolist 係 price searcher，入場門檻高，細公司仍然可以喺主導公司旁邊存在；主導地位、interdependence 同 non-price competition 先係真正特徵。

prompt_en: Put in order what happens when one dominant sneaker importer cuts its price:
prompt_zh: 排出一間主導波鞋入口商減價之後發生嘅次序：
items_en: one firm cuts its price to grab a bigger market share|the rival dominant firms notice the cut within days|the rivals cut their prices to match it|market shares end up roughly where they started|every firm earns less, so the firms avoid price cuts and compete by advertising instead
items_zh: 一間公司減價想搶大啲市場份額|其他主導對手幾日內就發現咗|對手跟住減價對撼|市場份額最後同原本差唔多|個個都賺少咗，所以之後唔敢減價，改為用廣告競爭
hint_en: Who reacts first, and what is left for the firm that cut its price?
hint_zh: 邊個先反應？最初減價嗰間最後剩返啲咩？
explain_en: This chain is why oligopoly prices are rigid and why non-price competition dominates: matched cuts return the shares but lower every firm's revenue.
explain_zh: 呢條鏈就解釋到點解 oligopoly 價錢 rigid、non-price competition 咁普遍：大家一齊減，份額返返原位，但每間嘅收入都低咗。

prompt_en: (Fictional) On the sneaker street, three large importers supply about 85 per cent of a popular type of basketball shoe, and about 20 tiny shops share the rest. Opening a new importing business needs a very large amount of capital. Which structure is this?
prompt_zh: （虛構）喺波鞋街，三間大入口商供應緊某款熱門籃球鞋大約 85%，餘下由大約 20 間細舖分。要開一間新嘅入口生意需要好大筆資本。呢個係咩結構？
options_en: perfect competition|oligopoly|monopoly|monopolistic competition
options_zh: perfect competition|oligopoly|monopoly|monopolistic competition
hint_en: Does the presence of 20 small shops change who actually dominates the market?
hint_zh: 有 20 間細舖，會唔會改變到實際上邊個主導緊個市場？
explain_en: Oligopoly means a few DOMINANT sellers with high entry barriers; small sellers may still exist, and 85 per cent in three hands with heavy capital needs fits the definition.
explain_zh: Oligopoly 係指幾間主導賣家加高入場門檻；細賣家一樣可以存在，三間佔 85% 再加要好多資本，正好符合定義。

prompt_en: (Fictional) On a fictional sneaker street the three biggest importers hold 40 per cent, 30 per cent and 15 per cent of the market. Together the top three hold ____ per cent of the market, which points to an ____.
prompt_zh: （虛構）喺虛構波鞋街，三大入口商分別佔市場 40%、30% 同 15%。三間加埋佔 ① 個百分比，呢個指向一個 ②。
options_en: 85|55|oligopoly|monopoly
options_zh: 85|55|oligopoly|monopoly
hint_en: Add the three shares first, then ask whether one seller or a few sellers dominate.
hint_zh: 先加埋三個份額，再諗吓係一個賣家定幾個賣家主導？
explain_en: 40 plus 30 plus 15 is 85; a few dominant sellers sharing most of the market is oligopoly, while monopoly would need one seller with no close substitute.
explain_zh: 40 加 30 加 15 等於 85；幾間主導賣家瓜分大部分市場就係 oligopoly，monopoly 就要一個冇 close substitute 嘅唯一賣家。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each move made by the three dominant sneaker importers this season:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將三間主導波鞋入口商今季嘅做法分類：
options_en: price competition|non-price competition
options_zh: price competition|non-price competition
items_en: cutting the wholesale price of a model by 10 per cent|sponsoring a schools basketball tournament|offering a two-year free repair service on every pair|giving retailers a $30 rebate on each pair sold|putting up large advertising posters along the street
items_zh: 將一款鞋嘅批發價減 10%|贊助一個學界籃球比賽|每對鞋送兩年免費維修服務|每賣出一對，回贈零售商 $30|沿街掛大幅廣告海報
hint_en: Does the buyer end up paying a different amount, or getting something extra?
hint_zh: 買家最後俾嘅錢數有冇變？定係佢攞多咗啲嘢？
explain_en: Rebates and wholesale price cuts change what is paid, so they are price competition; sponsorship, service and advertising are the non-price methods oligopolists prefer because price cuts are matched.
explain_zh: 回贈同減批發價改變咗俾出嘅錢，所以係 price competition；贊助、服務同廣告就係 oligopolist 偏好嘅 non-price 方法，因為減價對手一定跟。

prompt_en: (Fictional) One of the three dominant sneaker importers cuts its price by 10 per cent on a Monday. By Wednesday the other two have cut theirs by 10 per cent as well, and by the end of the month all three sell about the same quantity as before but earn less. This best illustrates:
prompt_zh: （虛構）三間主導波鞋入口商其中一間喺星期一減價 10%。到星期三另外兩間都減咗 10%，到月尾三間賣出嘅數量同之前差唔多，但賺少咗。呢個最能說明：
options_en: free entry and exit|homogeneous goods|interdependence, which is why oligopoly prices tend to be rigid|perfect market information among buyers
options_zh: 自由進出市場|homogeneous goods|interdependence，亦解釋到點解 oligopoly 嘅價錢傾向 rigid|買家之間嘅 perfect market information
hint_en: Did the first firm gain anything once the others reacted?
hint_zh: 當其他兩間反應之後，第一間有冇賺到嘢？
explain_en: Because each firm's outcome depends on the rivals' reaction, a matched price cut returns the shares and lowers everyone's revenue, so firms leave prices alone.
explain_zh: 因為每間公司嘅結果取決於對手反應，大家一齊減價之後份額照舊、收入齊跌，所以之後冇人再郁個價。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A student says: there are 20 small sneaker shops on the street as well as the three big importers, so this market cannot be an oligopoly. The best reply is:
prompt_zh: （虛構）有同學話：街上除咗三間大入口商仲有 20 間細鞋舖，所以呢個市場唔可能係 oligopoly。最好嘅回應係：
options_en: he is right, because an oligopoly must have only a few firms in total|he is wrong, because oligopoly means a few DOMINANT sellers and small sellers may still exist|he is right, because 23 sellers means monopolistic competition|he is wrong, because 23 sellers means perfect competition
options_zh: 佢啱，因為 oligopoly 總共只可以有幾間公司|佢錯，因為 oligopoly 係指幾間主導賣家，細賣家一樣可以存在|佢啱，因為 23 個賣家即係 monopolistic competition|佢錯，因為 23 個賣家即係 perfect competition
hint_en: Does the definition count every seller, or look at who holds most of the market?
hint_zh: 個定義係數晒所有賣家，定係睇邊個佔咗市場大部分？
explain_en: Oligopoly is judged by dominance and market share, not by a head count: a few sellers holding most of the market behind high entry barriers is enough.
explain_zh: 判斷 oligopoly 睇嘅係主導地位同市場份額，唔係數人頭：幾個賣家喺高門檻保護下佔咗大部分市場就夠。

prompt_en: A monopolist is the single seller of a good that has no close substitute.
prompt_zh: Monopolist 係一件冇 close substitute 嘅貨品嘅唯一賣家。
hint_en: Is being the only seller enough, or must the good also be hard to replace?
hint_zh: 淨係做唯一賣家夠唔夠？件貨係咪仲要好難搵嘢代替？
explain_en: The definition has two halves: one seller only, and no close substitute available to buyers; both must hold.
explain_zh: 個定義有兩半：得一個賣家，同埋買家搵唔到 close substitute；兩樣都要成立。

prompt_en: A monopolist can choose the price and the quantity sold at the same time.
prompt_zh: Monopolist 可以同時揀價錢同賣出嘅數量。
hint_en: Once the monopolist names a price, who decides how many units are actually bought?
hint_zh: Monopolist 開咗個價之後，實際買幾多件係邊個話事？
explain_en: A monopolist still faces a downward-sloping demand curve: it may set the price or the quantity, but buyers then determine the other one.
explain_zh: Monopolist 一樣面對向下斜嘅 demand curve：佢可以定價或者定量，但另一樣就由買家決定。

prompt_en: Because a monopolist faces a downward-sloping demand curve, it must lower its price if it wants to sell more.
prompt_zh: 因為 monopolist 面對向下斜嘅 demand curve，想賣多啲就一定要減價。
hint_en: What does a downward-sloping demand curve say about price and quantity demanded?
hint_zh: 向下斜嘅 demand curve 講緊價錢同 quantity demanded 有咩關係？
explain_en: Along a downward-sloping demand curve a larger quantity can only be sold at a lower price, so even a monopolist faces the law of demand.
explain_zh: 沿住向下斜嘅 demand curve，要賣多啲就一定要減價，所以連 monopolist 都逃唔出 law of demand。

prompt_en: Which of the following is NOT a source of monopoly power?
prompt_zh: 以下邊一項唔係 monopoly power 嘅來源？
options_en: a patent on a new invention|a franchise granted by the government|free entry into the market|exclusive ownership of a key resource
options_zh: 一項新發明嘅 patent|政府批出嘅 franchise|自由進入市場|獨家擁有一種關鍵資源
hint_en: Which item makes it EASIER, not harder, for a rival to appear?
hint_zh: 邊一項係令對手更容易出現，而唔係更難？
explain_en: Patents, franchises, exclusive ownership of a key resource, natural monopoly and collusion or integration all block rivals; free entry does the opposite.
explain_zh: Patent、franchise、獨家擁有關鍵資源、natural monopoly 同 collusion 或 integration 都擋住對手；自由入場啱啱相反。

prompt_en: A natural monopoly arises because:
prompt_zh: Natural monopoly 出現係因為：
options_en: the good is produced out of natural resources|the government orders that there be only one seller|the firm holds a patent on the product|one firm can supply the whole market at a lower average cost thanks to huge economies of scale
options_zh: 件貨用天然資源造|政府命令只可以有一個賣家|間公司攞咗件貨嘅 patent|因為有巨大嘅 economies of scale，一間公司供應成個市場嘅平均成本更低
hint_en: Would two firms each serving half the market cost more or less per unit?
hint_zh: 兩間公司各供應一半市場，每單位成本會高啲定低啲？
explain_en: A natural monopoly comes from huge economies of scale making a single supplier the cheapest way to serve the whole market; a government order is a statutory grant and a patent is a separate source.
explain_zh: Natural monopoly 嚟自巨大 economies of scale，令單一供應商成為服務成個市場最平嘅方法；政府命令係 statutory grant，patent 又係另一個來源。

prompt_en: Why can a patent create monopoly power?
prompt_zh: 點解 patent 可以製造 monopoly power？
options_en: it lowers the firm's production cost|it gives the holder the exclusive right to produce the product for a period, keeping rivals out|it forces buyers to buy the product|it makes the product homogeneous
options_zh: 佢令間公司嘅生產成本下降|佢俾持有人喺一段時間內獨家生產嘅權利，擋住對手|佢逼買家一定要買|佢令件貨變成 homogeneous
hint_en: What exactly does a patent stop other firms from doing?
hint_zh: Patent 到底阻止咗其他公司做咩？
explain_en: A patent or copyright is a legal entry barrier: for its term nobody else may produce the protected product, so the holder stays the single seller.
explain_zh: Patent 或者 copyright 係一種法律上嘅入場門檻：喺有效期內冇其他人可以生產受保護嘅產品，所以持有人維持做唯一賣家。

prompt_en: A flower shop is the only flower shop in a small town, but three other flower shops sit ten minutes away in the next town. The shop is:
prompt_zh: 一間花店係一個細鎮入面唯一嘅花店，但隔籬鎮十分鐘路程有三間花店。呢間舖係：
options_en: a monopoly, because it is the only shop in the town|a natural monopoly|not a monopoly, because close substitutes are easily available nearby|an oligopolist
options_zh: monopoly，因為佢係鎮入面唯一嘅舖|natural monopoly|唔係 monopoly，因為附近好易搵到 close substitute|oligopolist
hint_en: How far will a buyer go before the other shops count as substitutes?
hint_zh: 買家要行幾遠，其他舖先算係 substitute？
explain_en: Monopoly requires no close substitute, and shops ten minutes away are close substitutes; being the only shop within some boundary is not enough.
explain_zh: Monopoly 要求冇 close substitute，而十分鐘路程嘅舖就係 close substitute；喺某個範圍內做唯一一間並唔足夠。

prompt_en: A monopoly is a market with a ____ seller of a good that has no close ____.
prompt_zh: Monopoly 係一個市場，入面得 ① 賣家，賣嘅貨冇 close ②。
options_en: single|few|substitute|complement
options_zh: 單一|少數|substitute|complement
hint_en: How many sellers, and what must buyers be unable to find?
hint_zh: 有幾多個賣家？買家又搵唔到啲咩？
explain_en: Both halves of the definition matter: a few sellers would be oligopoly, and a close substitute would destroy the monopoly power even with one seller.
explain_zh: 定義兩半都重要：幾個賣家就係 oligopoly，而就算得一個賣家，有 close substitute 都會令 monopoly power 消失。

prompt_en: Monopoly power may come from a government ____ such as a franchise, or from huge economies of scale which produce a ____ monopoly.
prompt_zh: Monopoly power 可以嚟自政府嘅 ①，例如 franchise，又或者嚟自巨大嘅 economies of scale，形成一個 ② monopoly。
options_en: grant|loan|natural|legal
options_zh: 授權|貸款|natural|legal
hint_en: Which source comes from the law, and which comes from the shape of costs?
hint_zh: 邊個來源嚟自法律？邊個嚟自成本結構？
explain_en: A statutory grant or franchise is a legal source of monopoly power; huge economies of scale give a natural monopoly, where one supplier serves the market at the lowest average cost.
explain_zh: Statutory grant 或者 franchise 係法律上嘅 monopoly power 來源；巨大 economies of scale 就造成 natural monopoly，由一個供應商以最低平均成本服務成個市場。

prompt_en: Sort each source of monopoly power by where the power comes from:
prompt_zh: 將以下 monopoly power 嘅來源，按權力由邊度嚟分類：
options_en: from the law or the government|from costs or resources|from an agreement or a merger among firms
options_zh: 嚟自法律或者政府|嚟自成本或者資源|嚟自公司之間嘅協議或者合併
items_en: a statutory franchise to operate the only tunnel|a patent on a newly invented water filter|exclusive ownership of the only spring that yields a mineral water|huge economies of scale that make one supplier the cheapest|all the existing sellers colluding to act as a single seller|several firms integrating into one so that only one seller is left
items_zh: 營運唯一一條隧道嘅法定 franchise|一個新發明濾水器嘅 patent|獨家擁有出產某種礦泉水嘅唯一泉眼|巨大 economies of scale 令一個供應商最平|所有現有賣家 collude，扮成一個賣家咁行動|幾間公司 integrate 成一間，最後只剩一個賣家
hint_en: Ask who or what created the barrier in each case.
hint_zh: 逐個諗吓，道門檻係邊個或者咩造成？
explain_en: Franchises and patents are statutory grants, exclusive resources and huge economies of scale come from costs and resources, and collusion or integration is created by the firms themselves.
explain_zh: Franchise 同 patent 係法定授權，獨家資源同巨大 economies of scale 嚟自成本同資源，collusion 或 integration 就係啲公司自己搞出嚟。

prompt_en: Sort each case by whether it is a monopoly:
prompt_zh: 將以下個案按係咪 monopoly 分類：
options_en: a monopoly|not a monopoly
options_zh: 係 monopoly|唔係 monopoly
items_en: the sole supplier of piped water in a city where no alternative supply exists|the largest sneaker shop on a street where twenty other shops also sell sneakers|the only firm allowed by law to run the ferry to an island with no other transport|the busiest flower shop in a flower market full of flower shops|the holder of a patent on the only machine that can make a special fish tank filter
items_zh: 喺一個冇任何替代供應嘅城市入面唯一嘅自來水供應商|喺一條仲有二十間舖賣波鞋嘅街上最大嗰間|法律上唯一准許經營去某島渡輪嘅公司，而嗰島冇其他交通|喺一個滿街花店嘅花墟入面生意最好嗰間|持有唯一一部可以製造特別魚缸濾芯機器嘅 patent 嘅公司
hint_en: Is there any close substitute the buyer can turn to?
hint_zh: 買家仲有冇 close substitute 可以揀？
explain_en: Being the biggest or the busiest is not monopoly power; monopoly needs a single seller and no close substitute, usually protected by a very high entry barrier.
explain_zh: 做到最大或者最旺唔等於有 monopoly power；monopoly 要求得一個賣家、冇 close substitute，通常仲有好高嘅入場門檻保護住。

prompt_en: Put in order what happens when the only seller of a rare orchid raises its price:
prompt_zh: 排出唯一賣某種稀有蘭花嘅賣家加價之後發生嘅次序：
items_en: the monopolist decides to raise its price|buyers move up along the downward-sloping demand curve|the quantity bought falls|the monopolist finds that it cannot choose the price and the quantity at the same time
items_zh: monopolist 決定加價|買家沿住向下斜嘅 demand curve 向上移|買到嘅數量減少|monopolist 發現自己唔可以同時揀價錢同數量
hint_en: After the price is set, who decides how many pots are actually bought?
hint_zh: 價錢定咗之後，實際買幾多盆係邊個話事？
explain_en: Even a monopolist faces a downward-sloping demand curve, so setting the price hands the quantity decision to buyers; price and quantity cannot both be chosen.
explain_zh: 連 monopolist 都要面對向下斜嘅 demand curve，所以一定咗價，數量就交返俾買家決定；價同量唔可以兩樣都揀。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A government grants one company the sole right to supply piped gas to a new town for twenty years, and no other firm may lay pipes there. The source of this company's monopoly power is:
prompt_zh: （虛構）政府批俾一間公司獨家權利，二十年內供應煤氣俾一個新市鎮，其他公司唔准喺嗰度鋪管。呢間公司嘅 monopoly power 來源係：
options_en: exclusive ownership of a key resource|a patent on a new invention|collusion among the existing sellers|a franchise granted by the government
options_zh: 獨家擁有關鍵資源|一項新發明嘅 patent|現有賣家之間嘅 collusion|政府批出嘅 franchise
hint_en: Who created the barrier that stops other firms laying pipes?
hint_zh: 阻止其他公司鋪管嘅門檻，係邊個造出嚟？
explain_en: A statutory grant of an exclusive right to serve an area is a franchise; no resource, invention or agreement among firms is involved here.
explain_zh: 法定授予喺某地區獨家經營嘅權利就係 franchise；呢度唔涉及資源、發明或者公司之間嘅協議。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each fictional Hong Kong firm by the source of its monopoly power:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將以下虛構香港公司，按佢哋 monopoly power 嘅來源分類：
options_en: patent or copyright|exclusive ownership of a key resource|government grant or franchise
options_zh: patent 或 copyright|獨家擁有關鍵資源|政府授權或 franchise
items_en: a firm holding the patent on a new type of aquarium filter|a company owning the only quarry that yields a special white stone|the only operator licensed by the government to run an airport bus route|a publisher holding the copyright on a series of study notes|a firm that has bought up every supplier of a rare orchid bulb|the sole company granted a franchise to run a cross-harbour tunnel
items_zh: 持有一款新魚缸濾芯 patent 嘅公司|擁有唯一出產某種白石嘅石礦場嘅公司|政府唯一發牌經營機場巴士線嘅營運商|持有一套溫習筆記 copyright 嘅出版商|買起晒所有稀有蘭花球莖供應商嘅公司|獲批 franchise 經營過海隧道嘅唯一公司
hint_en: Ask whether the barrier is an invention protected by law, a thing the firm owns, or a permission from the state.
hint_zh: 諗吓道門檻係受法律保護嘅發明、公司擁有嘅實物，定係政府批嘅許可？
explain_en: Patents and copyrights protect creations, exclusive ownership blocks rivals from getting the input, and franchises or statutory grants are permissions only the government can give.
explain_zh: Patent 同 copyright 保護創作，獨家擁有令對手攞唔到投入品，franchise 或 statutory grant 就係只有政府先批得出嘅許可。

prompt_en: (Fictional) The only stall selling a rare orchid in the flower market sells 100 pots a week at $20 each. When it lowers the price to $16, it sells 150 pots a week. Its total revenue at $16 is $____, which shows that even a monopolist faces a ____-sloping demand curve.
prompt_zh: （虛構）花墟唯一賣某種稀有蘭花嘅檔，每星期用 $20 賣出 100 盆。減價到 $16 之後，每星期賣到 150 盆。喺 $16 嘅 total revenue 係 $①，可見連 monopolist 都面對 ② 斜嘅 demand curve。
options_en: 2,400|3,000|downward|upward
hint_en: Multiply the new price by the new quantity, then ask why the quantity changed at all.
hint_zh: 用新價乘新數量，再諗吓點解個數量會變？
explain_en: 16 times 150 is 2,400; the quantity sold rises only when the price falls, which is exactly what a downward-sloping demand curve means for a monopolist.
explain_zh: 16 乘 150 等於 2,400；要減價先賣得多，正正就係 monopolist 面對向下斜 demand curve 嘅意思。

prompt_en: (Fictional) The same orchid stall raises its price from $20 to $26 and finds it now sells only 60 pots a week instead of 100. Which statement is correct?
prompt_zh: （虛構）同一檔蘭花檔將價錢由 $20 加到 $26，發現每星期只賣到 60 盆，唔再係 100 盆。以下邊句正確？
options_en: it is no longer a monopolist, because it lost customers|a monopolist cannot force buyers to keep buying the same quantity at a higher price|a monopolist should never change its price|this proves that close substitutes must exist
options_zh: 佢唔再係 monopolist，因為走咗客|monopolist 唔可以逼買家喺高價下照買一樣咁多|monopolist 永遠都唔應該改價|呢個證明咗一定有 close substitute
hint_en: Does losing some buyers mean the seller is no longer the only seller?
hint_zh: 走咗啲客，係咪等於個賣家唔再係唯一賣家？
explain_en: A monopolist remains the single seller but still faces the law of demand along a downward-sloping demand curve, so a higher price always means a smaller quantity bought.
explain_zh: Monopolist 依然係唯一賣家，但一樣要沿住向下斜嘅 demand curve 受 law of demand 限制，價高就一定買得少。

prompt_en: (Fictional) In a fictional new town, one firm can supply all 10,000 households with piped water at an average cost of $4 per household, while two firms each serving 5,000 households would each face an average cost of $7. This is a case of:
prompt_zh: （虛構）喺一個虛構新市鎮，一間公司可以用每戶 $4 嘅平均成本供水俾全部 10,000 戶；如果兩間公司各服務 5,000 戶，每間嘅平均成本會係 $7。呢個係：
options_en: a natural monopoly created by huge economies of scale|a monopoly created by a patent|an oligopoly with two dominant firms|perfect competition between the two firms
options_zh: 由巨大 economies of scale 造成嘅 natural monopoly|由 patent 造成嘅 monopoly|有兩間主導公司嘅 oligopoly|兩間公司之間嘅 perfect competition
hint_en: Compare the cost per household when one firm serves everyone with the cost when the market is split.
hint_zh: 比較吓一間公司服務晒所有人同分開兩間嘅每戶成本？
explain_en: Average cost falls from $7 to $4 when output is concentrated in one firm, so huge economies of scale make a single supplier the cheapest arrangement, which is a natural monopoly.
explain_zh: 產量集中喺一間公司，平均成本由 $7 跌到 $4，即係巨大 economies of scale 令單一供應商最平，呢個就係 natural monopoly。

prompt_en: A price taker must accept the market price and cannot sell anything at a price above it.
prompt_zh: Price taker 一定要接受 market price，賣貴過個市場價就一件都賣唔出。
hint_en: If identical goods are on sale next door at the market price, who would pay you more?
hint_zh: 隔籬用 market price 賣緊一模一樣嘅貨，邊個會俾多啲錢你？
explain_en: A price taker has no price-setting power: the quantity demanded above the market price is zero because identical goods are available elsewhere at that price.
explain_zh: Price taker 冇定價能力：賣貴過 market price 嘅 quantity demanded 係零，因為第二度用個市場價就買到一模一樣嘅貨。

prompt_en: A price searcher faces a downward-sloping demand curve.
prompt_zh: Price searcher 面對一條向下斜嘅 demand curve。
hint_en: When a price searcher raises its price, does the quantity it sells stay the same?
hint_zh: Price searcher 加價之後，佢賣到嘅數量會唔會一樣？
explain_en: A price searcher sells less when it charges more and more when it charges less, which is exactly a downward-sloping demand curve.
explain_zh: Price searcher 收貴啲就賣少啲、收平啲就賣多啲，呢個就係向下斜嘅 demand curve。

prompt_en: Only a monopolist can be a price searcher.
prompt_zh: 只有 monopolist 先可以係 price searcher。
hint_en: Can a Ladies Street stall with its own design choose its own price?
hint_zh: 女人街一檔有自己設計嘅檔口，揀唔揀到自己個價？
explain_en: Sellers under monopolistic competition and oligopoly are price searchers too; only sellers under perfect competition are price takers.
explain_zh: Monopolistic competition 同 oligopoly 之下嘅賣家一樣係 price searcher；只有 perfect competition 之下嘅賣家先係 price taker。

prompt_en: In which market structure is every seller a price taker?
prompt_zh: 邊種市場結構之下，每個賣家都係 price taker？
options_en: monopoly|oligopoly|monopolistic competition|perfect competition
options_zh: monopoly|oligopoly|monopolistic competition|perfect competition
hint_en: Where are the goods homogeneous and each seller tiny?
hint_zh: 邊種結構之下啲貨係 homogeneous，每個賣家又好細？
explain_en: Only perfect competition combines homogeneous goods, very many tiny sellers and perfect information, leaving no seller any power over price.
explain_zh: 只有 perfect competition 同時有 homogeneous goods、非常多細賣家同完全資訊，令冇一個賣家對個價有話事權。

prompt_en: A price searcher that raises its price will:
prompt_zh: Price searcher 加價之後會：
options_en: lose all of its customers at once|lose some but not all of its customers|keep exactly the same number of customers|gain customers
options_zh: 即刻走晒所有客|走咗一部分客，但唔會走晒|客量完全唔變|多咗客
hint_en: If buyers see the goods as somewhat different, will every buyer leave?
hint_zh: 如果買家覺得啲貨有啲唔同，係咪個個都會走？
explain_en: Because a price searcher's good is not a perfect substitute for the rivals' goods, a higher price drives away some buyers but leaves others, which is what a downward-sloping demand curve shows.
explain_zh: 因為 price searcher 嘅貨同對手嘅貨唔係完美替代品，加價趕走部分買家但仲有人留低，呢個就係向下斜 demand curve 嘅意思。

prompt_en: Which pair is correctly matched?
prompt_zh: 以下邊一對配對得啱？
options_en: perfect competition and heavy advertising by each seller|monopoly and price taker|monopolistic competition and non-price competition|oligopoly and free entry into the market
options_zh: perfect competition 同每個賣家落重本賣廣告|monopoly 同 price taker|monopolistic competition 同 non-price competition|oligopoly 同自由進入市場
hint_en: Check each pair against the four conditions of the structure named.
hint_zh: 逐對對返嗰種結構嘅條件嚟睇吓？
explain_en: Monopolistic competition relies on packaging, service, location and advertising; perfect competition needs no advertising, a monopolist is a price searcher and oligopoly has high entry barriers.
explain_zh: Monopolistic competition 靠包裝、服務、地點同廣告；perfect competition 唔使賣廣告，monopolist 係 price searcher，oligopoly 嘅入場門檻高。

prompt_en: Why does an individual seller under perfect competition have almost no reason to advertise his own stall?
prompt_zh: 點解 perfect competition 之下嘅個別賣家，幾乎冇理由為自己檔口賣廣告？
options_en: advertising is banned in such markets|the goods are homogeneous and he can already sell all he wants at the market price|the sellers are too poor to pay for advertising|buyers have no information about the market
options_zh: 呢類市場禁止賣廣告|啲貨係 homogeneous，而佢用 market price 想賣幾多都賣到|啲賣家窮到俾唔起廣告費|買家對個市場一無所知
hint_en: What would an advertisement have to say when every stall sells the identical good at the same price?
hint_zh: 當每檔都用同一個價賣一模一樣嘅貨，個廣告仲可以講咩？
explain_en: With homogeneous goods there is nothing to distinguish and the price taker can sell his whole output at the market price, so advertising adds cost without adding sales.
explain_zh: 貨品 homogeneous 就冇嘢可以突出，而 price taker 用 market price 已經賣得晒，賣廣告只會加成本唔會加銷量。

prompt_en: A seller who must accept the market price is a ____, while a seller who faces a downward-sloping demand curve and looks for the price that suits it is a ____.
prompt_zh: 一定要接受 market price 嘅賣家係 ①，而面對向下斜 demand curve、搵啱自己個價嘅賣家就係 ②。
options_en: price taker|price searcher|monopolist|oligopolist
options_zh: price taker|price searcher|monopolist|oligopolist
hint_en: Which seller has a say over his own price, and which one does not?
hint_zh: 邊個賣家對自己個價有話事權？邊個冇？
explain_en: The dividing line is the shape of the demand curve facing the seller: horizontal at the market price gives a price taker, downward-sloping gives a price searcher.
explain_zh: 分界線係個賣家面對嘅 demand curve 形狀：喺 market price 水平就係 price taker，向下斜就係 price searcher。

prompt_en: Cutting the price of the goods is ____ competition, while competing through advertising, packaging, service and shop location is ____ competition.
prompt_zh: 減低貨品價錢係 ① competition，而用廣告、包裝、服務同舖位地點嚟競爭就係 ② competition。
options_en: price|non-price|free|perfect
options_zh: price|non-price|free|perfect
hint_en: Ask whether the amount of money the buyer pays has changed.
hint_zh: 問吓買家俾出嘅錢數有冇變？
explain_en: Price competition works through the price itself; non-price competition attracts buyers while the price stays where it is, and it dominates under monopolistic competition and oligopoly.
explain_zh: Price competition 直接用個價；non-price competition 就係喺價錢不變下吸客，喺 monopolistic competition 同 oligopoly 最普遍。

prompt_en: Sort each seller by the price role it plays:
prompt_zh: 將以下賣家按佢扮演嘅價格角色分類：
options_en: price taker|price searcher
options_zh: price taker|price searcher
items_en: a stall in a market of very many stalls selling identical goldfish|the single seller of a good with no close substitute|a Ladies Street stall selling bags of its own design|one of the few dominant firms in an oligopoly|a seller under perfect competition
items_zh: 喺一個好多檔賣一模一樣金魚嘅市場入面嘅一檔|一件冇 close substitute 嘅貨品嘅唯一賣家|女人街一檔賣自己設計嘅袋|oligopoly 入面幾間主導公司之一|perfect competition 之下嘅賣家
hint_en: Can this seller raise its price and still sell something?
hint_zh: 呢個賣家加咗價之後，仲賣唔賣得出嘢？
explain_en: Only perfect competition produces price takers; monopolistic competition, oligopoly and monopoly all face downward-sloping demand curves and so are price searchers.
explain_zh: 只有 perfect competition 之下嘅賣家先係 price taker；monopolistic competition、oligopoly 同 monopoly 都面對向下斜 demand curve，所以全部係 price searcher。

prompt_en: Sort each market structure by the number and size of its sellers:
prompt_zh: 將以下市場結構按賣家數目同規模分類：
options_en: one seller|a few dominant sellers|many or very many sellers
options_zh: 一個賣家|幾個主導賣家|好多或者非常多賣家
items_en: monopoly|oligopoly|perfect competition|monopolistic competition|the only firm allowed by law to run a tunnel|three firms supplying most of a city's network service
items_zh: monopoly|oligopoly|perfect competition|monopolistic competition|法律上唯一可以經營一條隧道嘅公司|三間公司供應全市大部分網絡服務
hint_en: Count the sellers, and ask whether a few of them hold most of the market.
hint_zh: 數吓幾多個賣家，再諗吓係咪得幾個佔咗大部分市場？
explain_en: The four structures are ordered by sellers: one in monopoly, a few dominant ones in oligopoly, many in monopolistic competition and very many in perfect competition.
explain_zh: 四種結構按賣家排：monopoly 一個，oligopoly 幾個主導，monopolistic competition 好多，perfect competition 非常多。

prompt_en: Put the four market structures in order from the LEAST to the MOST price-setting power:
prompt_zh: 將四種市場結構由定價能力最細排到最大：
items_en: perfect competition|monopolistic competition|oligopoly|monopoly
items_zh: perfect competition|monopolistic competition|oligopoly|monopoly
hint_en: Start with the structure whose sellers must simply accept the market price.
hint_zh: 由賣家淨係可以接受 market price 嗰種開始諗？
explain_en: Price-setting power rises as the number of sellers falls and entry barriers rise: none for a price taker, a little where goods are differentiated, more with a few dominant firms, most for a single seller with no close substitute.
explain_zh: 賣家愈少、入場門檻愈高，定價能力就愈大：price taker 完全冇，貨品 differentiated 有少少，幾間主導公司再多啲，冇 close substitute 嘅唯一賣家最大。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each fictional Mong Kok seller by its price role:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將以下虛構旺角賣家按佢嘅價格角色分類：
options_en: price taker|price searcher
options_zh: price taker|price searcher
items_en: one of 80 stalls all selling the same common goldfish at $8|the only stall in the flower market selling a rare orchid with no substitute|a Ladies Street stall selling scarves printed with its own design|one of three importers supplying most of the sneakers on the sneaker street|a stall selling plain plastic fish bags identical to those of 50 other stalls
items_zh: 80 檔之中一檔，全部用 $8 賣同一種普通金魚|花墟入面唯一賣一款冇 substitute 稀有蘭花嘅檔|女人街一檔賣印住自己設計嘅頸巾|三間供應波鞋街大部分波鞋嘅入口商之一|一檔賣同另外 50 檔一模一樣嘅普通膠魚袋
hint_en: Ask whether the seller would still sell anything after raising its price by a dollar.
hint_zh: 諗吓呢個賣家加一蚊之後，仲賣唔賣得出嘢？
explain_en: A seller of homogeneous goods among very many sellers must accept the market price; differentiation or dominance gives a downward-sloping demand curve and so price-searching power.
explain_zh: 喺非常多賣家之中賣 homogeneous goods 嘅賣家一定要接受 market price；有差異化或者主導地位就會面對向下斜 demand curve，有 price searching 能力。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A Ladies Street stall raises the price of its own design of scarf from $30 to $35. Weekly sales fall from 200 to 170 pieces, and the stall keeps trading. This shows that the stall is:
prompt_zh: （虛構）女人街一檔將自己設計嘅頸巾由 $30 加到 $35。每星期銷量由 200 條跌到 170 條，檔口照做生意。呢個顯示呢檔係：
options_en: a price taker, because sales fell|a monopolist, because it raised its price|a price searcher, because it lost some but not all of its buyers|in perfect competition, because other stalls sell scarves too
options_zh: price taker，因為銷量跌咗|monopolist，因為佢加咗價|price searcher，因為佢走咗部分客但唔係全部|處於 perfect competition，因為其他檔都賣頸巾
hint_en: Compare this result with what would happen to a stall selling goods identical to everyone else's.
hint_zh: 同一檔賣同人哋一模一樣貨品嘅檔口比較吓，結果會點？
explain_en: A price taker would sell nothing above the market price; losing only part of the buyers shows a downward-sloping demand curve, and having rivals rules out monopoly.
explain_zh: Price taker 賣貴過 market price 就一件都賣唔出；只走咗部分買家即係面對向下斜 demand curve，而有對手就唔會係 monopoly。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Using the same scarf stall, total revenue before the price rise was 30 times 200, that is $6,000. After the rise it is 35 times 170, that is $____, so the stall's total revenue ____ even though it could still choose its own price.
prompt_zh: （虛構）用返同一檔頸巾檔，加價前 total revenue 係 30 乘 200，即 $6,000。加價後係 35 乘 170，即 $①，所以就算佢揀到自己個價，total revenue 都 ②。
options_en: 5,950|7,000|falls|rises
hint_en: Work out the new price times the new quantity before comparing with $6,000.
hint_zh: 先計新價乘新數量，再同 $6,000 比較？
explain_en: 35 times 170 is 5,950, which is below 6,000; a price searcher may set its price but the quantity then falls along the demand curve, so a price rise can reduce total revenue.
explain_zh: 35 乘 170 等於 5,950，低過 6,000；price searcher 可以定價，但數量會沿住 demand curve 跌，所以加價可以令 total revenue 減少。

prompt_en: (Fictional) On the goldfish street, 80 stalls all sell exactly the same common goldfish at $8. Ah Sing's stall marks its fish at $9 and sells none all day. Ah Sing's stall is best described as:
prompt_zh: （虛構）金魚街有 80 檔全部用 $8 賣同一種普通金魚。成哥檔標價 $9，成日一條都賣唔出。成哥檔最好形容為：
options_en: a price taker facing a horizontal demand curve at $8|a price searcher with a little price-setting power|a monopolist of its own fish|one of a few dominant sellers
options_zh: 喺 $8 面對水平 demand curve 嘅 price taker|有少少定價能力嘅 price searcher|自己啲魚嘅 monopolist|幾間主導賣家之一
hint_en: Why did the quantity sold fall all the way to zero rather than just a little?
hint_zh: 點解賣出嘅數量直頭跌到零，而唔係跌少少？
explain_en: Homogeneous goods and perfect information make the demand curve facing each tiny seller horizontal at the market price, so nothing sells above $8.
explain_zh: 貨品 homogeneous 加資訊完全，令每個細賣家面對嘅 demand curve 喺 market price 位置係水平，所以貴過 $8 就一件都賣唔出。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each competitive move made by four different Mong Kok sellers:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將四個唔同旺角賣家嘅競爭做法分類：
options_en: price competition|non-price competition
options_zh: price competition|non-price competition
items_en: a sneaker importer sponsoring a street basketball event|a goldfish stall matching the $8 charged by every other stall|a flower stall offering free delivery within the district|a scarf stall cutting its price from $35 back to $30|a bag stall giving every buyer a printed cloth pouch
items_zh: 一間波鞋入口商贊助街頭籃球活動|一檔金魚檔跟足其他檔嘅 $8|一檔花檔提供區內免費送貨|一檔頸巾檔將價錢由 $35 減返 $30|一檔袋檔送印花布袋俾每位買家
hint_en: Does the buyer hand over a different amount of money, or receive something extra?
hint_zh: 買家俾出嘅錢數有冇變？定係佢多攞咗啲嘢？
explain_en: Moves that change the money paid are price competition; sponsorship, delivery and free gifts attract buyers while the price stands, and non-price methods dominate wherever goods are differentiated.
explain_zh: 改變咗俾出嘅錢就係 price competition；贊助、送貨同贈品係喺價錢不變下吸客，而貨品有差異嘅市場最常用 non-price 方法。

prompt_en: In economics the usual assumption is that a firm aims at the largest possible profit.
prompt_zh: 喺 economics 入面，一般假設間公司嘅目標係賺到最大嘅 profit。
hint_en: When economists explain how a firm behaves, which objective do they normally start from?
hint_zh: 經濟學家解釋一間公司點做嘢嘅時候，通常由邊個目標出發？
explain_en: Profit maximisation is the usual assumption about the objective of firms; market share, corporate social responsibility, non-profit provision and survival are the other objectives a firm may hold.
explain_zh: Profit maximisation 係對公司目標嘅一般假設；market share、corporate social responsibility、non-profit provision 同 survival 就係公司可能有嘅其他目標。

prompt_en: A shop that aims at a larger market share must also be earning the largest possible profit this year.
prompt_zh: 一間以更大 market share 為目標嘅舖頭，今年一定同時賺緊最大嘅 profit。
hint_en: To take customers away from a rival, what does a shop usually have to do to its price?
hint_zh: 想搶對手啲客，舖頭通常要對個價錢做啲咩？
explain_en: A firm chasing market share often cuts its price or spends heavily on promotion, giving up profit now in the hope of a larger share of buyers later.
explain_zh: 追 market share 嘅公司通常減價或者狂落廣告，即係放棄咗而家嘅 profit，博將來佔多啲買家。

prompt_en: Because a non-profit-making organisation does not aim at profit, it has no objective at all.
prompt_zh: 因為 non-profit-making organisation 唔係為咗賺錢，所以佢根本冇目標。
hint_en: If a free study room is not chasing profit, what is it trying to do with its money?
hint_zh: 一間免費自修室唔係為賺錢，咁佢啲錢想做到啲咩？
explain_en: Non-profit provision is itself an objective: the organisation aims to provide a service, and charges at most enough to cover its costs.
explain_zh: Non-profit provision 本身就係一個目標：個機構嘅目標係提供服務，最多只收夠成本嘅費用。

prompt_en: Which of the following is the USUAL assumption about the objective of a firm in economics?
prompt_zh: 喺 economics 入面，對一間公司目標嘅一般假設係以下邊項？
options_en: the largest profit|the largest quantity of output|the largest total revenue|the largest market share
options_zh: 最大嘅 profit|最大嘅產量|最大嘅 total revenue|最大嘅 market share
hint_en: Is a firm trying to be the biggest seller, or trying to be the best off?
hint_zh: 間公司係想做最大嗰個，定係想自己最著數？
explain_en: The standard assumption is profit maximisation. Largest output, largest total revenue and largest market share are different targets and usually give a different answer.
explain_zh: 標準假設係 profit maximisation。最大產量、最大 total revenue、最大 market share 係另外三個目標，通常會得出唔同嘅答案。

prompt_en: (Setting) A sneaker shop on 波鞋街 sells every pair at a very low price for a whole year so as to pull customers away from a newly opened rival, even though it earns much less this year. Its objective is best described as:
prompt_zh: （情境）波鞋街一間波鞋舖成年都賣到好平，為咗搶新開嘅對手啲客，就算今年賺少好多都照做。佢嘅目標最啱嘅描述係：
options_en: profit maximisation|market share|corporate social responsibility|non-profit provision
options_zh: profit maximisation|market share|corporate social responsibility|non-profit provision
hint_en: What is the shop buying with the profit it gives up?
hint_zh: 間舖用放棄咗嘅 profit 去換返啲咩？
explain_en: Giving up current profit in order to serve a larger proportion of the buyers on the street is the market share objective.
explain_zh: 放棄而家嘅 profit，去爭取服務條街更大比例嘅買家，就係 market share 呢個目標。

prompt_en: (Setting) A computer shop in a 旺角 computer centre gives part of its takings to a neighbourhood study room and packs every order in recycled boxes. This behaviour is an example of:
prompt_zh: （情境）旺角電腦中心一間電腦舖，將部分收入捐畀街坊自修室，又用回收紙盒包貨。呢種做法係以下邊項嘅例子？
options_en: market share|survival|profit maximisation|corporate social responsibility
options_zh: market share|survival|profit maximisation|corporate social responsibility
hint_en: Who benefits from the boxes and the donation, the shop or the neighbourhood?
hint_zh: 啲回收盒同捐款，係間舖著數定街坊著數？
explain_en: Corporate social responsibility means the firm takes the interests of society and the environment into account, not only its own profit.
explain_zh: Corporate social responsibility 即係間公司唔淨係諗自己嘅 profit，仲會考慮社會同環境嘅利益。

prompt_en: (Setting) Business on 女人街 is very bad this year. A stall owner cuts his own pay, opens shorter hours and takes any order that covers his bills, just so that the stall is still there next year. His objective is:
prompt_zh: （情境）今年女人街生意好差。一個檔主減自己人工、縮短營業時間，只要夠支付開支嘅單就照接，為嘅係出年檔口仲喺度。佢嘅目標係：
options_en: market share|survival|profit maximisation|corporate social responsibility
options_zh: market share|survival|profit maximisation|corporate social responsibility
hint_en: What is the smallest thing a firm can still be aiming at when times are bad?
hint_zh: 生意差嘅時候，一間公司最起碼仲可以追求啲咩？
explain_en: When conditions are bad a firm may aim only at survival, that is at staying in business, rather than at the largest profit.
explain_zh: 環境差嘅時候，公司可能淨係追求 survival，即係捱得住繼續做落去，而唔係追求最大 profit。

prompt_en: The usual assumption in economics is that a firm aims at ____ maximisation, but a firm that cuts its price mainly to take customers away from its rivals is aiming at a larger ____.
prompt_zh: Economics 嘅一般假設係公司追求 ① maximisation；但如果一間公司減價主要係為咗搶對手啲客，佢追求嘅就係更大嘅 ②。
options_en: profit|market share|survival|corporate social responsibility
options_zh: profit|market share|survival|corporate social responsibility
hint_en: Which objective is the starting point, and which one is paid for by giving up profit?
hint_zh: 邊個目標係出發點？邊個目標要用放棄 profit 去換？
explain_en: Profit maximisation is the standard assumption; taking customers from rivals by pricing low is the market share objective, which costs the firm some current profit.
explain_zh: Profit maximisation 係標準假設；用低價搶對手啲客就係 market share 目標，要蝕返部分而家嘅 profit。

prompt_en: A clinic run by a charity that charges only enough to cover its costs is an example of ____ provision, while a shop that keeps trading at a loss during a slump only in order to stay open is aiming at ____.
prompt_zh: 由慈善團體營運、只收夠成本費用嘅診所，係 ① provision 嘅例子；而喺市道差嘅時候蝕住都照做、淨係想捱落去嘅舖頭，目標就係 ②。
options_en: non-profit|survival|market share|profit
options_zh: non-profit|survival|market share|profit
hint_en: One of them never wanted profit, while the other one wants profit but cannot get it right now. Which is which?
hint_zh: 一個由頭到尾都唔係為 profit，另一個想要 profit 但而家攞唔到。你覺得邊個係邊個？
explain_en: Non-profit provision means the organisation exists to provide the service, not to earn profit. Survival means the firm still wants profit but is first trying to stay in business.
explain_zh: Non-profit provision 即係個機構存在係為咗提供服務，唔係為賺 profit。Survival 即係間公司仲想要 profit，但第一步係要保住盤生意。

prompt_en: Sort each action by the objective it shows:
prompt_zh: 將以下每個行動，按佢反映嘅目標分類：
options_en: market share|corporate social responsibility|survival
options_zh: market share|corporate social responsibility|survival
items_en: selling below the usual price for a whole year to pull customers from a new rival|sorting the shop waste for recycling and giving free lessons to neighbourhood children|cutting the owner's own pay and opening shorter hours during a slump just to keep the shop open|spending heavily on advertising to become the seller with the most customers on the street|selling the delivery van to pay this month's rent and stay in business|paying suppliers who treat their workers well even though they charge a bit more
items_zh: 成年賣平過平時嘅價，搶新對手啲客|將舖頭垃圾分類回收，又免費教街坊細路|市道差時減自己人工、縮短營業時間，淨係想間舖唔執笠|大手落廣告，想做條街客最多嗰間|賣咗部送貨車去交今個月租，撐住盤生意|寧願貴少少，都幫襯善待工人嘅供應商
hint_en: Is the firm fighting for customers, looking after society, or just trying to stay alive?
hint_zh: 間公司係喺度爭客、照顧社會，定係淨係想生存落去？
explain_en: Market share actions buy customers with profit, corporate social responsibility actions take society and the environment into account, and survival actions aim only at staying in business.
explain_zh: Market share 嘅行動係用 profit 買客；corporate social responsibility 嘅行動係考慮社會同環境；survival 嘅行動淨係為咗保住盤生意。

prompt_en: Sort each organisation by whether it aims at profit:
prompt_zh: 將以下機構按佢係咪以 profit 為目標分類：
options_en: profit-making firm|non-profit-making organisation
options_zh: 以 profit 為目標嘅公司|non-profit-making organisation
items_en: a goldfish shop on 金魚街 owned by a trader who keeps everything it earns|a charity that runs a free study room for students|a family sneaker stall that tries to earn as much as it can|a hostel run by a school that charges only enough to cover its costs|a flower stall in 花墟 whose owner takes home all the takings|a neighbourhood association that collects fees only to cover its expenses
items_zh: 金魚街一間由商人擁有、賺幾多攞幾多嘅金魚舖|一個為學生辦免費自修室嘅慈善團體|一檔想賺到盡嘅家庭式波鞋檔|一間由學校營運、只收夠成本費用嘅宿舍|花墟一檔，檔主將全部收入袋落自己袋|一個只收夠開支費用嘅街坊會
hint_en: After the bills are paid, does anybody take the surplus home?
hint_zh: 畀晒啲開支之後，有冇人會將剩低嘅錢袋落自己袋？
explain_en: A profit-making firm exists to earn profit for its owners; a non-profit-making organisation exists to provide a service and charges at most enough to cover its costs.
explain_zh: 以 profit 為目標嘅公司，存在係為老闆賺 profit；non-profit-making organisation 存在係為提供服務，最多只收夠成本。

prompt_en: Which statement about the objectives of firms is CORRECT?
prompt_zh: 以下關於公司目標嘅陳述，邊項正確？
options_en: every firm must aim at maximum profit, so no other objective is possible|corporate social responsibility means the firm is not allowed to earn any profit|a firm aiming at survival must be earning the largest possible profit|a firm aiming at market share may give up some profit today in the hope of serving more buyers later
options_zh: 每間公司都一定追求最大 profit，唔可能有其他目標|Corporate social responsibility 即係間公司唔可以賺 profit|以 survival 為目標嘅公司，一定賺緊最大嘅 profit|追求 market share 嘅公司，可能放棄今日部分 profit，博將來服務多啲買家
hint_en: Can a firm hold an objective other than profit maximisation, and what does that objective cost it?
hint_zh: 公司可唔可以有 profit maximisation 以外嘅目標？呢個目標要佢付出啲咩？
explain_en: Profit maximisation is only the usual assumption, not a rule. Market share is bought with current profit; corporate social responsibility can sit beside profit; survival is what a firm falls back on when profit is out of reach.
explain_zh: Profit maximisation 只係一般假設，唔係規矩。Market share 要用而家嘅 profit 去換；corporate social responsibility 可以同賺 profit 並存；survival 係賺唔到 profit 時嘅退一步目標。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ah Sing opens a goldfish shop on 金魚街 in 1995. For the first year he sells every tank set $30 below what the other shops charge, and tells his wife he expects to earn almost nothing this year but to have the most regular customers on the street by 1997. His objective in the first year is:
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿成 1995 年喺金魚街開咗間金魚舖。頭一年每套魚缸都平過其他舖 $30，佢同老婆講今年預咗賺咩都冇，但 1997 年之前要做到條街熟客最多嗰間。佢第一年嘅目標係：
options_en: profit maximisation|non-profit provision|market share|survival
options_zh: profit maximisation|non-profit provision|market share|survival
hint_en: What is he expecting to get back in exchange for this year's profit?
hint_zh: 佢預咗用今年嘅 profit，換返啲咩？
explain_en: Pricing below rivals and accepting almost no profit in order to hold the largest share of the street's buyers is the market share objective.
explain_zh: 賣平過對手、預咗幾乎冇 profit，為嘅係佔條街最大比例嘅買家，呢個就係 market share 目標。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort what each 旺角 business did in 1996 by the objective it shows:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將以下旺角商戶 1996 年所做嘅事，按佢反映嘅目標分類：
options_en: market share|corporate social responsibility|survival
options_zh: market share|corporate social responsibility|survival
items_en: a flower shop in 花墟 gives its unsold flowers to a home for the elderly every evening|a stall on 西洋菜街 halves its price for six months to become the biggest seller of cassette tapes on the street|a noodle shop borrows from a cousin to pay the rent after three bad months|a computer shop pays for a rubbish-free street campaign in its block|a sneaker shop advertises on every bus stop in the district to overtake the shop next door in number of buyers|a toy stall sells its display cabinet to cover this month's wages
items_zh: 花墟一間花舖每晚將賣剩嘅花送去老人院|西洋菜街一檔減價一半半年，想做條街賣卡式帶最多嘅一檔|一間麵舖捱咗三個月淡市，向表哥借錢交租|一間電腦舖出錢搞佢嗰幢大廈嘅清潔街道運動|一間波鞋舖喺區內每個巴士站落廣告，想喺買家數目上越過隔籬舖|一檔玩具檔賣咗陳列櫃，去出今個月人工
hint_en: Is the business fighting for customers, looking after the neighbourhood, or just trying to last another month?
hint_zh: 間舖係爭客、照顧街坊，定係淨係想捱多一個月？
explain_en: Market share actions spend profit to win buyers, corporate social responsibility actions serve society or the environment, and survival actions are taken only to keep the business open.
explain_zh: Market share 嘅行動係用 profit 換買家；corporate social responsibility 嘅行動係服務社會或環境；survival 嘅行動淨係為咗間舖繼續開到。

prompt_en: (Fictional) The Wong Family Trust runs a reading room above 旺角街市 and charges each member $20 a month, which is just enough to cover the electricity and the rent. Two streets away, Mr Ho keeps his loss-making watch stall open through a bad year by living on his savings, hoping trade will return. The reading room is an example of ____ provision and Mr Ho is aiming at ____.
prompt_zh: （虛構）黃氏家族信託喺旺角街市樓上辦咗間閱讀室，每位會員收 $20 一個月，啱啱夠畀電費同租金。隔兩條街，何生喺淡市年頭蝕住都唔收檔，靠食老本撐住，希望生意返返嚟。閱讀室係 ① provision 嘅例子，而何生嘅目標係 ②。
options_en: non-profit|survival|market share|profit
options_zh: non-profit|survival|market share|profit
hint_en: One of them never wanted a surplus, while the other one wants profit but cannot get it this year. Which is which?
hint_zh: 一個由頭到尾都唔想有盈餘，另一個想賺 profit 但今年賺唔到。你覺得邊個係邊個？
explain_en: Charging only enough to cover costs is non-profit provision; staying open at a loss in order to still be in business later is the survival objective.
explain_zh: 只收夠成本嘅費用就係 non-profit provision；蝕住都繼續做、為咗將來仲有得做，就係 survival 目標。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ms Lam sells handbags at a 女人街 stall. She switches to a supplier whose bags are the same quality but $12 cheaper each, and she raises the price of her best-selling bag by $5 after finding that her customers still buy just as many. Which objective best explains BOTH decisions?
prompt_zh: （虛構）林小姐喺女人街賣手袋。佢轉咗用一個每個袋平 $12、質素一樣嘅供應商；又發現啲客照買咁多，所以將最好賣嗰款加價 $5。以下邊個目標最能解釋呢兩個決定？
options_en: profit maximisation|market share|corporate social responsibility|non-profit provision
options_zh: profit maximisation|market share|corporate social responsibility|non-profit provision
hint_en: Both moves push the same number in the same direction. Which number is it?
hint_zh: 兩個決定都將同一個數推向同一個方向。你覺得係邊個數？
explain_en: Cutting cost per bag and raising price where quantity sold does not fall both widen the gap between total revenue and total cost, which is exactly profit maximisation.
explain_zh: 減低每個袋嘅成本，同埋喺銷量唔跌嘅地方加價，兩樣都拉闊 total revenue 同 total cost 之間嘅距離，正正就係 profit maximisation。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A shop in a 旺角 computer centre gives 10 cents of every dollar it takes to a neighbourhood study room. A student concludes that the shop therefore cannot be a profit-making firm at all.
prompt_zh: （虛構）旺角電腦中心一間舖，每收一蚊就捐一毫子畀街坊自修室。有個學生因此話，呢間舖根本唔可能係以 profit 為目標嘅公司。
hint_en: Can a firm care about the neighbourhood and about its own profit at the same time?
hint_zh: 一間公司可唔可以同時關心街坊同自己嘅 profit？
explain_en: Corporate social responsibility is an objective a profit-making firm can pursue alongside profit; only an organisation that exists to provide a service without aiming at profit is a non-profit-making organisation.
explain_zh: Corporate social responsibility 係一間以 profit 為目標嘅公司都可以同時追求嘅目標；只有為提供服務而存在、唔以 profit 為目標嘅機構，先至係 non-profit-making organisation。

prompt_en: Total revenue equals the price of the good multiplied by the quantity sold.
prompt_zh: Total revenue 等於件貨嘅 price 乘以賣出嘅 quantity。
hint_en: If you sell 10 fish at $5 each, how do you work out what you took in?
hint_zh: 賣咗 10 條魚，每條 $5，你點計收到幾多錢？
explain_en: TR = P x Q. Take the price the buyer pays and multiply it by the number of units actually sold.
explain_zh: TR = P x Q。將買家付嘅 price 乘以實際賣出嘅單位數量。

prompt_en: The output that gives the largest total revenue must also be the output that gives the largest profit.
prompt_zh: 帶嚟最大 total revenue 嘅產量，一定同時係 profit 最大嘅產量。
hint_en: When you sell more, does anything else rise along with total revenue?
hint_zh: 賣多啲嘅時候，除咗 total revenue，仲有咩會一齊升？
explain_en: Profit = TR - TC, so a larger TR that comes with an even larger TC gives a smaller profit. The largest TR does not mean the largest profit.
explain_zh: Profit = TR - TC，所以 TR 大咗但 TC 大得更多，profit 反而細咗。最大 TR 唔代表最大 profit。

prompt_en: Profit is what is left after total cost is taken away from total revenue.
prompt_zh: Profit 係 total revenue 減走 total cost 之後剩低嘅嘢。
hint_en: Which two totals does a shop owner compare at the end of the day?
hint_zh: 舖頭老闆收工嗰陣係比較邊兩個總數？
explain_en: Profit = TR - TC. Both sides must be totals for the SAME output, otherwise the subtraction means nothing.
explain_zh: Profit = TR - TC。兩邊都要係同一個產量嘅總數，唔係嘅話個減數冇意思。

prompt_en: A goldfish shop on 金魚街 sells 30 goldfish in a day at $8 each. Its total revenue for the day is:
prompt_zh: 金魚街一間金魚舖一日賣咗 30 條金魚，每條 $8。佢嗰日嘅 total revenue 係：
hint_en: Do you add the price and the quantity, or multiply them?
hint_zh: 係將 price 同 quantity 相加，定係相乘？
explain_en: TR = P x Q = 8 x 30 = 240. Adding the price to the quantity is a common slip and gives a figure with no meaning.
explain_zh: TR = P x Q = 8 x 30 = 240。將 price 加 quantity 係常見錯誤，得出嚟嘅數冇意義。

prompt_en: A flower stall in 花墟 takes in $900 in a day and its total cost for the day is $650. Its profit for the day is:
prompt_zh: 花墟一檔花檔一日收到 $900，嗰日嘅 total cost 係 $650。佢嗰日嘅 profit 係：
hint_en: Which of the two figures is taken away from the other?
hint_zh: 兩個數之中，邊個減邊個？
explain_en: Profit = TR - TC = 900 - 650 = 250. The $900 is total revenue, not profit, because the costs have not yet been paid out of it.
explain_zh: Profit = TR - TC = 900 - 650 = 250。$900 係 total revenue 而唔係 profit，因為啲成本仲未喺入面扣。

prompt_en: A stall keeps this record. At an output of 1 basket TR is $40 and TC is $25; at 2 baskets TR is $75 and TC is $45; at 3 baskets TR is $105 and TC is $70; at 4 baskets TR is $130 and TC is $105. At which output is profit largest?
prompt_zh: 一檔檔口有以下記錄。產量 1 籃時 TR 係 $40、TC 係 $25；2 籃時 TR 係 $75、TC 係 $45；3 籃時 TR 係 $105、TC 係 $70；4 籃時 TR 係 $130、TC 係 $105。邊個產量嘅 profit 最大？
options_en: 1 basket|2 baskets|3 baskets|4 baskets
hint_en: Work out TR minus TC at every output before you choose.
hint_zh: 揀之前，將每個產量嘅 TR 減 TC 都計一次。
explain_en: The profits are 15, 30, 35 and 25, so profit is largest at 3 baskets even though TR is largest at 4 baskets.
explain_zh: 四個產量嘅 profit 分別係 15、30、35、25，所以 3 籃嘅 profit 最大，雖然 4 籃嘅 TR 最大。

prompt_en: A 花墟 stall records this. At 10 bunches TR is $200 and TC is $120; at 20 bunches TR is $360 and TC is $250; at 30 bunches TR is $480 and TC is $400; at 40 bunches TR is $560 and TC is $560. Which statement is CORRECT?
prompt_zh: 花墟一檔記錄如下。10 紮時 TR 係 $200、TC 係 $120；20 紮時 TR 係 $360、TC 係 $250；30 紮時 TR 係 $480、TC 係 $400；40 紮時 TR 係 $560、TC 係 $560。以下邊項正確？
options_en: TR rises with output, so profit also rises with output|profit is largest at 40 bunches because TR is largest there|profit is the same at every output because TR and TC both rise|profit is largest at 20 bunches, although TR is largest at 40 bunches
options_zh: TR 隨產量上升，所以 profit 都隨產量上升|profit 喺 40 紮時最大，因為嗰度 TR 最大|每個產量嘅 profit 都一樣，因為 TR 同 TC 都係上升|profit 喺 20 紮時最大，雖然 TR 喺 40 紮時最大
hint_en: TR keeps rising here, but what is happening to the gap between TR and TC?
hint_zh: 呢度 TR 一直升，但 TR 同 TC 之間嘅距離變咗點？
explain_en: The profits are 80, 110, 80 and 0. TR rises at every step, yet the gap TR - TC is widest at 20 bunches and has closed completely at 40 bunches.
explain_zh: 四個產量嘅 profit 分別係 80、110、80、0。TR 每一步都升，但 TR - TC 嘅距離喺 20 紮時最闊，去到 40 紮就完全收窄到零。

prompt_en: Total revenue equals ____ multiplied by the quantity sold, and profit equals total revenue minus ____.
prompt_zh: Total revenue 等於 ① 乘以賣出嘅數量；profit 等於 total revenue 減 ②。
options_en: price|total cost|marginal cost|average cost
options_zh: price|total cost|marginal cost|average cost
hint_en: Which cost figure covers everything the firm spent on that output?
hint_zh: 邊個成本數字包晒間公司喺嗰個產量上洗嘅所有錢？
explain_en: TR = P x Q and profit = TR - TC. Marginal cost is the cost of one extra unit and average cost is cost per unit, so neither can be subtracted from a total.
explain_zh: TR = P x Q，profit = TR - TC。Marginal cost 係多做一單位嘅成本，average cost 係每單位成本，兩者都唔可以直接由一個總數度減走。

prompt_en: A 女人街 stall sells 25 scarves at $12 each, so its total revenue is $____. If its total cost is $220, its profit is $____.
prompt_zh: 女人街一檔賣咗 25 條頸巾，每條 $12，所以 total revenue 係 $①。如果 total cost 係 $220，profit 就係 $②。
hint_en: Which comes first, the multiplying or the subtracting?
hint_zh: 先乘定先減？諗吓次序。
explain_en: TR = 12 x 25 = 300, then profit = 300 - 220 = 80. Adding TR and TC instead of subtracting gives 520, which is a common slip.
explain_zh: TR = 12 x 25 = 300，再計 profit = 300 - 220 = 80。將 TR 同 TC 相加而唔係相減會得出 520，係常見錯誤。

prompt_en: Sort each statement about revenue and profit:
prompt_zh: 將以下關於 revenue 同 profit 嘅陳述分類：
options_en: correct|wrong
options_zh: 正確|錯誤
items_en: TR equals price times quantity sold|profit equals TR minus TC|the output with the largest TR always gives the largest profit|TR can rise while profit falls|profit equals TR plus TC|TR is zero when nothing is sold
items_zh: TR 等於 price 乘賣出數量|profit 等於 TR 減 TC|TR 最大嘅產量一定 profit 最大|TR 可以上升嘅同時 profit 下跌|profit 等於 TR 加 TC|乜都賣唔出嘅時候 TR 等於零
hint_en: Check each one against the two formulas TR = P x Q and profit = TR - TC.
hint_zh: 用 TR = P x Q 同 profit = TR - TC 兩條式，逐句檢查。
explain_en: Profit is the gap between TR and TC, so it is a subtraction, and a rising TR tells you nothing about profit until TC is brought in.
explain_zh: Profit 係 TR 同 TC 之間嘅距離，所以係減數；TR 升緊本身講唔到 profit 點，要睇埋 TC。

prompt_en: Sort each day's trading by its result:
prompt_zh: 將以下每日嘅買賣結果分類：
options_en: made a profit|made a loss
options_zh: 賺咗|蝕咗
items_en: TR $500 and TC $420|TR $260 and TC $310|TR $1,000 and TC $850|TR $700 and TC $760|TR $180 and TC $95|TR $640 and TC $690
hint_en: Is TR bigger than TC, or the other way round?
hint_zh: 係 TR 大過 TC，定係反過來？
explain_en: Profit = TR - TC. A positive answer is a profit and a negative answer is a loss; the size of TR on its own decides nothing.
explain_zh: Profit = TR - TC。答案係正數就係賺，負數就係蝕；單睇 TR 有幾大係決定唔到嘅。

prompt_en: Put the steps for working out a day's profit from a stall's record in order:
prompt_zh: 將由檔口記錄計出一日 profit 嘅步驟排好次序：
items_en: read the price of the good and the quantity sold|multiply price by quantity to get total revenue|read the total cost of that same output|take total cost away from total revenue to get profit
items_zh: 讀出件貨嘅 price 同賣出嘅數量|將 price 乘數量，得出 total revenue|讀出同一個產量嘅 total cost|用 total revenue 減 total cost，得出 profit
hint_en: Which total has to exist before you can subtract anything from it?
hint_zh: 要減嘢之前，邊個總數要先計出嚟？
explain_en: TR must be built from P and Q first; only then can the TC of the SAME output be taken away to leave profit.
explain_zh: 要先用 P 同 Q 砌返 TR；之後先可以減走同一個產量嘅 TC，剩低嘅就係 profit。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ah Man runs a goldfish stall on 金魚街. On Sunday he sells 40 goldfish at $7 each, and his total cost for the day is $210. His profit on Sunday is:
prompt_zh: （虛構）阿文喺金魚街擺檔賣金魚。星期日佢賣咗 40 條金魚，每條 $7，嗰日嘅 total cost 係 $210。佢星期日嘅 profit 係：
hint_en: Build total revenue first, then bring in the cost.
hint_zh: 先砌返 total revenue，再計埋成本。
explain_en: TR = 7 x 40 = 280, so profit = 280 - 210 = 70. The $280 is total revenue and $490 comes from adding TR and TC instead of subtracting.
explain_zh: TR = 7 x 40 = 280，所以 profit = 280 - 210 = 70。$280 係 total revenue；$490 係將 TR 同 TC 相加而唔係相減得出嚟。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Ms Cheung keeps this record for her 波鞋街 stall. Selling 20 pairs gives TR $3,000 and TC $2,400; selling 30 pairs gives TR $4,200 and TC $3,700; selling 40 pairs gives TR $5,200 and TC $4,900. Which output should she choose if she wants the largest profit?
prompt_zh: （虛構）張小姐波鞋街檔口嘅記錄如下。賣 20 對時 TR 係 $3,000、TC 係 $2,400；賣 30 對時 TR 係 $4,200、TC 係 $3,700；賣 40 對時 TR 係 $5,200、TC 係 $4,900。如果佢想 profit 最大，應該揀邊個產量？
options_en: 40 pairs, because TR is largest there|30 pairs|20 pairs|any of them, because the profit is the same
options_zh: 40 對，因為嗰度 TR 最大|30 對|20 對|邊個都得，因為 profit 都一樣
hint_en: Work out TR minus TC at all three outputs before you choose.
hint_zh: 揀之前，三個產量嘅 TR 減 TC 都計一次。
explain_en: The profits are 600, 500 and 300, so 20 pairs gives the largest profit. Choosing 40 pairs is the classic mistake of reading the largest TR as the largest profit.
explain_zh: 三個產量嘅 profit 係 600、500、300，所以 20 對嘅 profit 最大。揀 40 對就係將最大 TR 當成最大 profit 嘅經典錯誤。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Uncle Yip sells 60 bunches of flowers in 花墟 on a festival morning at $25 a bunch, so his total revenue is $____. His total cost that morning is $1,180, so his profit is $____.
prompt_zh: （虛構）葉伯喺花墟一個節日早上賣咗 60 紮花，每紮 $25，所以 total revenue 係 $①。嗰個早上佢嘅 total cost 係 $1,180，所以 profit 係 $②。
hint_en: Multiply the price by the number of bunches first, then deal with the cost.
hint_zh: 先將 price 乘紮數，再處理成本。
explain_en: TR = 25 x 60 = 1,500, then profit = 1,500 - 1,180 = 320. Adding TR and TC gives 2,680, which is not a profit figure at all.
explain_zh: TR = 25 x 60 = 1,500，再計 profit = 1,500 - 1,180 = 320。將 TR 同 TC 相加得出 2,680，根本唔係 profit。

prompt_en: (Fictional) A fruit seller in 旺角街市 tells his neighbour that today was his best day of the year because he took in more money than on any other day, so his profit must also be the highest of the year.
prompt_zh: （虛構）旺角街市一個生果佬同隔籬檔講，今日收到嘅錢多過全年任何一日，所以今日一定係全年 profit 最高嘅一日。
hint_en: To take in that much money, what did he have to buy in the morning?
hint_zh: 要收到咁多錢，佢朝早要入幾多貨？
explain_en: Taking in more money is a larger TR, but stocking up for that busy day also raises TC; profit = TR - TC, so the highest TR need not be the highest profit.
explain_zh: 收到多啲錢即係 TR 大咗，但為咗旺日入多咗貨，TC 一樣會升；profit = TR - TC，所以 TR 最高唔一定 profit 最高。

prompt_en: (Fictional) Sort each day at a 西洋菜街 record stall by its result:
prompt_zh: （虛構）將西洋菜街一檔唱片檔每日嘅結果分類：
options_en: made a profit|made a loss
options_zh: 賺咗|蝕咗
items_en: Monday: sold 20 records at $40 each, total cost $650|Tuesday: sold 10 records at $40 each, total cost $520|Wednesday: sold 35 records at $40 each, total cost $1,200|Thursday: sold 15 records at $40 each, total cost $680
items_zh: 星期一：賣咗 20 張碟，每張 $40，total cost $650|星期二：賣咗 10 張碟，每張 $40，total cost $520|星期三：賣咗 35 張碟，每張 $40，total cost $1,200|星期四：賣咗 15 張碟，每張 $40，total cost $680
hint_en: Turn each day's sales into total revenue before you compare it with the cost.
hint_zh: 同成本比較之前，先將每日嘅銷量變成 total revenue。
explain_en: The TRs are 800, 400, 1,400 and 600 against costs of 650, 520, 1,200 and 680, so Monday and Wednesday show a profit while Tuesday and Thursday show a loss.
explain_zh: 四日嘅 TR 分別係 800、400、1,400、600，成本係 650、520、1,200、680，所以星期一同星期三賺，星期二同星期四蝕。

prompt_en: Under perfect competition a seller is a price taker, so its marginal revenue is equal to the market price at every output.
prompt_zh: 喺 perfect competition 之下，賣家係 price taker，所以佢喺每個產量嘅 marginal revenue 都等於市場價格。
hint_en: If the seller can sell any quantity at the same price, how much does selling one more unit bring in?
hint_zh: 如果賣家喺同一個價可以賣任何數量，咁多賣一件貨會收多幾多錢？
explain_en: A price taker must accept the market price and can sell any quantity at it, so each extra unit adds exactly that price to total revenue: MR = P.
explain_zh: Price taker 一定要接受市價，喺嗰個價可以賣任何數量，所以每多賣一件貨，total revenue 就加返正正嗰個價：MR = P。
